routes.label: Use the supplied difference bound and construct an attaining piecewise-linear function
Bound the difference and attain it

question: Consider functions \(f\) that satisfy \[|f(x)-f(y)|\leq \dfrac{1}{2}|x-y|\] for all real numbers \(x\) and \(y.\) Of all such functions that also satisfy the equation \(f(300) = f(900),\) what is the greatest possible value of the following expression? \[f(f(800))-f(f(400))\]
solution:
The equality \(f(300)=f(900)\) gives a common reference value close to both \(f(400)\) and \(f(800)\). This will bound the distance between the two inputs to the outer \(f\).

Let \(c=f(300)=f(900)\). The given inequality gives
\[
|f(400)-c|\le\frac12(400-300)=50,
\qquad
|f(800)-c|\le\frac12(900-800)=50.
\]
Two numbers that are each within \(50\) of \(c\) are at most \(100\) apart. Thus
\[
|f(800)-f(400)|
\le |f(800)-c|+|c-f(400)|
\le100.
\]
Applying the given inequality to the inputs \(f(800)\) and \(f(400)\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(f(800))-f(f(400))
&\le |f(f(800))-f(f(400))|\\
&\le\frac12|f(800)-f(400)|\\
&\le50.
\end{aligned}
\]
We must also show that some allowed function reaches \(50\).

Define \(f\) by connecting the following points, in order, with straight line segments:
\[
\begin{gathered}
(300,600),\ (400,550),\ (550,575),\\
(650,625),\ (800,650),\ (900,600).
\end{gathered}
\]
For \(x\le300\) and \(x\ge900\), set \(f(x)=600\). The five connecting segments have slopes
\[
-\frac12,\quad\frac16,\quad\frac12,\quad\frac16,\quad-\frac12,
\]
and the outside pieces are horizontal. Therefore, on every piece, the absolute change in \(f\) is at most half the change in the input. For inputs on different pieces, split the interval between them at the breakpoints and add these bounds. The total absolute change is still at most half the total interval length, so the required inequality holds for all real inputs.

This function has \(f(300)=f(900)=600\), and its specified values give
\[
f(f(800))-f(f(400))
=f(650)-f(550)
=625-575=50.
\]
Hence the greatest possible value is \(\boxed{50}\), choice B.
